- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and smooth out the slope.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum — raise forecast mean by 1–2% to align with sentiment bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead) — apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for short-term (1–7 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +0.3/-0.4), model exhibits erratic behavior — use moving average of last 5–7 days to stabilize forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize it — add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast for 3–7 day horizon.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility — reduce forecast variance by 10–15% if sentiment is stable or mildly negative.
